newsitem.title: CHINA: China market slide not seen hitting economy.
newsitem.headline: China market slide not seen hitting economy.

text.p: The steep slide on China's stock markets should not have a major impact on the nation's economy, financial specialists said on Tuesday.
"We don't expect a great fallout from the movements on the stock exchanges," said Jonathan Anderson, deputy representative in Beijing for the International Monetary Fund.
"Capitalisation is small," he told reporters. "They (the stock exchanges) will not play a large or real role in the economy" for some time.
That view was shared by World Bank chief of mission Pieter Bottelier, who said the minor role China's stock markets play in the economy would limit any possible impact.
"China's fledgling equity markets have a long way to go before they become more mature," he said.
Chinese regulatory authorities triggered a sell-off on domestic share markets on Monday with a tough editorial in the official People's Daily that warned of excessive speculation in the markets.
The editorial also accused big institutional traders of manipulating the market and lashed out at brokers for allowing improper overdrafts to pump up the market.
The Shanghai and Shenzhen share markets tumbled again on Tuesday after sliding sharply on Monday.
At midday, the Shenzhen A share index for domestic investors lost 9.93 percent, nearly falling its 10 percent daily limit, to 375.77. The Shanghai A share index was down 9.52 percent to 947.12.
